# Initial extraction

Created on 2026-09-14. The original applications are not migrated by this repository.

| Source | Revision | Extracted behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brighter-di/backend` | `46f3fdadf5b8be4cb953ca742d05a393b64af7b2` | Custom strategy validation, canonical rule identity, the backtest engine score builders, predicate lowering, weighted selection and semantic regression tests |
| Brighter Studio | `9be28522225d983e78db4019c9d172426464ac20` | Language specification, transport field definitions and 75 saved contract fixtures |
| `brighter-di/strategy-engine` | `962baec9fd0377533d7740051f88cb35aefe6c0a` | Reference for an independent Go parser of the Studio indentation grammar |

The 92 DSL language samples come from the backend's existing backtest-parity suite.
The standalone parser also supports Studio's case-insensitive spellings, singular
`day`, leading tabs and header-free fragments. Syntax diagnostics use one-based
positions. Parsing is separate from semantic readiness so consumers can inspect
incomplete allocation trees.

`testdata/backend-golden.json` was captured by running `CompileCustom` from the
actual backend against `testdata/studio-contract.json`, using a temporary Go test
overlay. No backend source file was changed. Each valid case stores its rule key
and the SHA-256 of sorted JSON for the compiled execution tree after recursively
removing `id`, `name` and `description`. Those fields carry presentation metadata
or fresh UUIDs; all allocation, condition, ranking and rebalance fields remain.
These fingerprints are intentionally frozen and are not regenerated by this package.

`testdata/research-tickers.json` is a frozen alias/underlying-symbol allowlist from
Studio's Ondo BNB catalog. It excludes currencies. It exists only in tests, keeping
asset availability and contract metadata outside the standalone language.

Differences made during extraction:

- Exported transport types are `Strategy` and `Node`; compiled results are `Compiled`.
- The runtime has no application imports, token registry, API client or database.
- Asset validation is caller policy through `Options.Tickers`; without an allowlist,
  syntactically valid symbols are accepted and canonicalized to uppercase.
- Compiled asset display names are their canonical symbols. Consumers supply their
  own asset labels; score node IDs remain fresh UUIDs.
- The public JSON ABI adds operation names, package/language versions and diagnostics.
- Formatting preserves semantic rule identity without editor-only IDs or hidden fields.
  It does not include Studio's reconciliation, autocomplete or indentation repair.
- The standalone grammar requires headers before rules. Canonical Studio documents
  already follow that order. Omitted headers use the documented fragment defaults.

Future adoption should first make brighterd import the native Go module and supply
its research-symbol allowlist. Studio can then use the Wasm loader for parsing,
formatting, validation and compilation, while retaining editor state reconciliation
and UI-specific completion features. Native the strategy tree imports, parameterized presets,
backtesting, market data, publishing and portfolio execution remain responsibilities
of their respective applications.

The npm package is scaffolded and can be packed locally. It has not been published
to an npm registry; the GitHub repository contains the standalone source and CI
builds the distributable Wasm artifacts.
